speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. To help me understand your chronic joint pain, can you tell me which specific joints are affected and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the involvement of the first metatarsophalangeal joint (great toe), hips, and knees, do you notice any visible redness, warmth, or swelling in these areas, especially in the morning?

text: My main symptom is Pain in the left great toe, hips, and knees. I also have Symptoms worsen with activity, Symptoms improve with rest.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of pain worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of osteoarthritis. To confirm this and assess the severity of the joint damage, I need to see your imaging results.

REQUEST IMAGES: X_Rays_of_hips_and_knees, X_Ray_of_left_great_toe.
REQUEST TEST: HbA1c (to check for diabetes which can sometimes coexist with neuropathic pain in the foot).
